title: Allowlist-driven network design + evidence automation
content:
Purpose:
This is a working doc describing an allowlist-first VPC segmentation pattern for Private deployments, associated minimal firewall rule sets, pragmatic mTLS placement, RBAC v2 surface mapping, and an evidence automation runbook for SIEM-friendly audit exports.

Audience:
- Eng: private deployments and infra
- Security: compliance and audit
- Solutions: customer acceptance testing (CAT)

High-level goals:
- Reduce attack surface via explicit allowlists and narrow subnets
- Produce deterministic, SIEM-ingestible audit artifacts for every config-change and network flow policy change
- Automate evidence packaging so customers and compliance teams can validate controls quickly
- Keep runtime latency and deployment complexity minimal (avoid heavy per-packet proxies where unnecessary)

Design principles (short):
- Allowlist-first: deny-by-default for all inter-service and ingress paths
- Least privilege segmentation: isolate control plane, model serving, management plane, and customer data lanes into separate subnets/VPCs
- Telemetry-first: every rule change emits a structured audit event, and flows of interest are sampled/forwarded to SIEM via egress-forwarder
- Reproducible infra: firewall and route configuration are generated from code (Terraform modules) and signed artifacts stored in artifact registry

Logical VPC layout (pattern):
- VPC root: rhd-priv-<tenant>-vpc
  - subnet-control-plane (management/control, private, no customer data)
  - subnet-serving (model inference nodes, GPU pools)
  - subnet-data (persistent store, s3-like gateways)
  - subnet-bastion (admin access pair, ephemeral jumpbox)
  - subnet-observability (metrics, logs, SIEM-forwarders)

Minimal firewall rule taxonomy (allowlist-driven examples):
- Ingress (customer-facing): 
  - Allow tcp/443 from customer-proxied-eips -> LB frontends only (TLS terminated upstream for hosted; private: mTLS required end-to-end)
- Control plane -> Serving: 
  - Allow tcp/8443 from subnet-control-plane -> subnet-serving (API control path)
- Serving -> Data: 
  - Allow tcp/9000 (object gateway) and tcp/5432 (postgres read-only) from subnet-serving -> subnet-data (only specific IP ranges and IAM service accounts)
- Observability: 
  - Allow tcp/10514 (syslog), tcp/9200 (es-ingest) from subnet-observability -> SIEM-forwarder
- Admin (bastion): 
  - Allow ssh/22 from corporate-vpn-ip-ranges -> subnet-bastion; no direct public SSH to serving nodes

Example cloud firewall rule (GCP-like) - declarative intent semantics (not raw CLI):
- name: allow-serving-to-data-objectgw
  direction: INGRESS
  priority: 1000
  action: ALLOW
  sourceRanges: ["10.10.3.0/24"]  # subnet-serving
  protocols: ["tcp:9000"]
  targetTags: ["subnet-data-gateway"]
  description: "Only serving nodes may reach data object gateway on 9000"

mTLS placement and pragmatic guidance:
- mTLS is required for any path that crosses tenant boundaries or carries PII/credentials. For internal control plane calls, prefer mTLS between service-to-service and use short-lived certs (K8s cert-manager or Istio CA).
- For high-throughput token paths (model inference), prefer edge TLS + authenticated connection tokens and local TLS for control flows to avoid per-token crypto overhead.
- Certificate lifecycle: describe rotation policy - certs rotate every 30 days, with automated rolling by terraform + orchestration job. Keep CRL and OCSP checks enabled for long-lived certs.

RBAC v2 mapping (surface-level):
- Roles (examples):
  - NetworkOperator: manage firewall rules, read-only view of VPC flow logs, approve network changes
  - InfraDeployer: apply Terraform modules for subnets and routes, cannot modify firewall rules without NetworkOperator approval
  - Observability: can create SIEM dashboards and create forwarder policies but cannot read keys
  - SupportReadOnly: read-only across network and audit logs (for customer support)
- Resources: firewall-rule, subnet, route, load-balancer, siem-forwarder, mTLS-cert
- Entitlements: use RBAC v2 to express "action on resource" tuples in the audit log as plain fields so SIEM can pivot easily (see audit schema below).

Audit log schema (flat, SIEM-friendly example):
- timestamp: 2024-03-04T12:23:45.123Z
- event_id: EV-20240304-00079
- actor_name: "l.moreno@example.com"
- actor_role: "NetworkOperator"
- action: "firewall.rule.update"
- resource_type: "firewall-rule"
- resource_id: "allow-serving-to-data-objectgw"
- before_hash: "sha256:..."  # optional
- after_hash: "sha256:..."
- change_delta: "+allow tcp/9000 from 10.10.3.0/24"
- approval_ticket: "jira:PD-2397"
- terraform_plan_id: "tfplan-20240304-87"
- evidence_uri: "s3://priv-deploy-evidence/PD-2397/plan.json"
- delivery_status: "forwarded-to-siem"
- signature: "sig:v1:..."

SIEM export mapping (Elasticsearch / SIEM fields to standardize):
- @timestamp -> timestamp
- host.user -> actor_name
- user.role -> actor_role
- event.action -> action
- network.resource -> resource_id
- change.* -> change_delta
- tags -> ["rbac-v2","allowlist","private-deploy"]

Example SIEM query examples (KQL / Splunk-ish):
- Find recent firewall changes by role:
  - splunk: search index=net_audit action=firewall.rule.update actor_role=NetworkOperator | stats count by actor_name, resource_id, _time
- Failed evidence deliveries (needs retries):
  - splunk: index=evidence delivery_status!=forwarded-to-siem | table event_id, evidence_uri, delivery_status, _time

Evidence automation runbook (prototype flow):
1) Change request: engineer opens Jira PD-2397 with terraform change and links PR (github:infra/.../pr/102).
2) CI: terraform plan -> plan is persisted to artifact-bucket s3://priv-deploy-evidence/PD-2397/plan.json; CI signs the artifact using build key and emits an audit event.
3) Approvals: NetworkOperator approves in Jira -> approval triggers automation to run terraform apply in ephemeral runner. Approval metadata included in audit event.
4) Apply: terraform apply produces state diff and output; state diff is stored and has before/after hashes. Apply emits structured audit event to audit-log service.
5) Forward: audit-log service normalizes payload and pushes to internal Kafka topic "audit-events". A consumer picks events tagged "network" and writes to SIEM-forwarder service which batches and sends to SIEM (Elastic/Splunk).
6) Evidence packaging: a nightly job collects all events per Jira ticket and packages them into a signed zip (evidence bundle) placed at s3://priv-deploy-evidence/<ticket>/evidence-bundle-<date>.zip and emits a proof event with signature.
7) Customer verification: A mapping file (evidence-index.json) is published alongside the bundle describing hashes and queries to reproduce the evidence in SIEM (KQL/Splunk).

Evidence artifact naming convention:
- <ticket>-<artifact-type>-<timestamp>-<short-hash>.json
- e.g., PD-2397-plan-20240304T122300Z-3f4b.json

Verification queries to include in evidence bundle (examples):
- Count of allowlist rules created in the last 7 days for tenant: 
  - ES DSL: {"query":{"bool":{"must":[{"term":{"event.action":"firewall.rule.create"}},{"term":{"tenant":"rhd-priv-123"}}]}}}
- SIEM proof (splunk): index=net_audit event_id=EV-20240304-00079 | table actor_name, action, change_delta, evidence_uri

Hardening checklist (operational items) - quick run before customer handoff:
- [ ] All subnets defined in Terraform modules and locked to module versions
- [ ] Firewall rules only declared via code; no manual console edits allowed (enforce via org policy)
- [ ] VPC Flow logs enabled at INFO and sampled at 100% for control plane subnets
- [ ] mTLS enforced on control-plane endpoints; cert rotation job active and monitored
- [ ] RBAC v2 roles mapped and no user has wildcard network perms
- [ ] SIEM forwarder reachable from subnet-observability and CA pinned
- [ ] Evidence bundling job test run completed and bundle signed
- [ ] SIEM ingestion tests passed (test event roundtrip < 60s)
- [ ] Canary test: deploy small tf change with ticket PD-TEST-ALLOW and validate audit-to-siem pipeline

Operational run notes / TODOs (short):
- TODO: define retention policy for evidence bundles (default: 365 days) and archive policy to cold storage after 90 days.
- TODO: prototype delta visualization UI for firewall diffs (front-end story for product)
- Question: do we want per-tenant dedicated SIEM indexes or a single index with tenant field? (security prefers per-tenant; ops prefers single for cost)
- Note: this doc intentionally kept example ports narrow — concrete production ports list to be added per customer template.

Backrefs / quick links:
- Compliance playbook (confluence): confluence:PD-compliance-evidence-playbook
- Terraform modules: github:infra/private-deploy-configs/tree/main/modules/network
- Jira (approval flow): jira:PD-2397

Appendix: small ASCII diagram (left-to-right)
  [External] --> [LB frontends] --> [subnet-serving] --> [subnet-data]
                          |
                          -> [subnet-observability] -> [SIEM-forwarder]
                          -> [subnet-control-plane]

End of working draft.
